headline: High: Cursor can write/egress broadly while PaddleOCR can process documents, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; PaddleOCR processes documents/images that could contain attacker-controlled text. If PaddleOCR output is copied into Cursor or stored in shared files, Cursor may treat it as trusted content. The pair has a filesystem bridge, so injection is plausible even without a documented direct channel.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is written into a Cursor-opened file or clipboard item
IF Cursor parses document text from a shared workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into Cursor prompts
Keep OCR outputs in a separate directory from Cursor workspaces
Add a manual review step before pasting OCR text into Cursor
Use provenance labels in filenames or comments
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance tracking between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. In a shared workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from PaddleOCR inputs into Cursor’s context and then out through Cursor’s model-provider or API calls. This is a default-path leakage risk because Cursor’s egress is broad and isolation is none.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document workspace
IF sensitive documents or images are processed by PaddleOCR and then opened in Cursor
IF Cursor sends those contents to external model providers
mitigations: Restrict Cursor to a non-sensitive workspace
Process sensitive documents only in an isolated directory
Turn off or limit network access for Cursor during OCR review
Redact documents before OCR processing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; PaddleOCR can call APIs and run browsers. If both operate on the same repository or document set, concurrent writes and uncoordinated edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The shared filesystem bridge in Cursor makes this a realistic conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same files or repository concurrently
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode while PaddleOCR writes derived artifacts into the same workspace
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Pause one agent before the other edits the repo
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents, and Cursor can consume that text in its agent loop and act on it with shell or git tools. If Cursor treats OCR output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commands. The pathway exists, but it is not inherently automatic because a human or workflow must pass outputs between them.
conditions: IF OCR output is used as direct input to Cursor’s agent loop
IF Cursor is allowed to execute shell or git actions based on extracted text
mitigations: Require human verification of OCR output before actioning it
Compare OCR text against the source document for critical fields
Limit Cursor to drafting changes, not executing them
Use a checksum or screenshot cross-check for key values
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and action

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, while Cursor can store open files, clipboard contents, and send data to external model providers. If regulated documents or EU PII are opened in Cursor after OCR, retention and residency obligations may diverge between the two tools. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF regulated documents, PHI, or EU PII are processed by PaddleOCR and then opened in Cursor
IF Cursor’s external model-provider calls retain or transmit that data
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Strip identifiers before OCR and editing
Keep compliance-sensitive files out of Cursor
Review vendor retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
